title: P0 Thundering Sessions - Connection Leak & Reconnect Storm Postmortem
body:
Summary:
On 2026-01-12 between 02:13–03:05 UTC we experienced a P0 outage impacting hosted inference streaming endpoints. Symptoms were large latency spikes for streaming responses, progressive increase in 5xxs on the stream ingest route, and client-side stalled streams. ~37% of streaming requests failed or timed out for 52 minutes at peak. The incident was resolved by an emergency mitigation at 02:43 UTC and fully recovered after rolling restart of the session-keeper fleet by 03:05 UTC.

Impact:
- Duration: ~52 minutes (partial mitigation at 02:43, full recovery by 03:05).
- Affected surface: streaming sessions on hosted inference (function-calling and long-lived chat streams).
- Client visible: stalled streams, reconnect loops from SDKs, increased 5xx and client timeouts.
- Business impact: several high-traffic customers observed degraded UX; SLO blips recorded.

Detection & Timeline (local times = UTC):
- 02:10: custom dashboard showed steady rise in ephemeral_worker_utilization and active_sessions_per_node.
- 02:13: alert SRE-STREAM-ERRORS fired (5xx rate on /v1/streams > 2% sustained).
- 02:16: on-call paged; initial hypothesis: upstream model hotpath regressions or autoscaler lag.
- 02:20: logs showed many streaming sessions in WAIT_FOR_CLIENT state with no traffic; connection counts on session-keeper did not drop.
- 02:25: spike in socket_fds_open and tcp_ephemeral_port_exhaustion warnings on edge proxies.
- 02:31: attempted soft mitigation — increased session idle timeout for new sessions; no immediate effect.
- 02:36: identified abnormal use of the session-keeper connection pool: aborted client connections were not releasing server-side session slot due to a bug in session-keeper's onDisconnect handler.
- 02:38: executed coordinated rolling restart of session-keeper small fraction (canary) — partial improvement.
- 02:43: rolled restart across all session-keeper pods; immediate drop in leaked session counts and 5xx rate started declining.
- 03:05: metrics normalized, streaming latency returned to baseline.

Root cause:
A bug introduced in stream-mux v2.14.0 changed the disconnect cleanup path: when a client aborted a stream during handshake or early in the stream lifecycle, session-keeper failed to decrement the active_session_count and did not close associated KV cache references. Over time these leaked sessions accumulated on a subset of pods until they exhausted the per-node session quota and ephemeral ports on the proxy, causing queuing and 5xx responses. The leak coupled with client SDKs' reconnect logic (aggressive exponential backoff misconfigured in a recent SDK) produced a reconnect storm — many clients repeatedly re-opened streams which rapidly consumed remaining capacity ("thundering sessions").

Contributing factors:
- Degraded visibility: the leaked sessions were accounted as HEALTHY in a metric that only tracked "accepted sockets", not completed/active logical sessions.
- No backpressure on control-plane connection creation: autoscaler treated socket acceptance as success and did not surface steady-state saturation.
- SDK behavior change: a client SDK release disabled jitter in reconnect backoff for streaming, increasing synchronization of reconnect attempts across clients.

Mitigation taken:
Immediate (hotfixes):
- 02:36: Increased aggressive alert thresholds and paged on-call.
- 02:38–02:43: Coordinated rolling restart of session-keeper fleet to reclaim leaked slots.
- 02:45: Temporarily increased per-node session quota and raised idle-eviction frequency for cache entries to accelerate recovery while restarts completed.

Longer-term fixes planned
(owners and ETA):
- INFRA-3421 (owner: Daniel Park, due 2026-02-05): Fix session-keeper disconnect path to always decrement active_session_count and garbage-collect KV cache references.
- SRE-8764 (owner: Riley Chen, due 2026-01-28): Add "logical active sessions" metric and dashboard to surface leaked sessions and their lifetime distributions.
- DEV-5587 (owner: Mateo Alvarez, due 2026-01-20): Patch SDK to reintroduce jitter in reconnect backoff and release a-compatible SDK patch + communication to top customers.
- SRE-8801 (owner: Priya Nair, due 2026-02-12): Add autoscaler gating on logical session metrics (not just socket accepts) to prevent scaling decisions from masking saturation.

Runbook / On-call playbook (draft snippets to add to SRE runbook):
- When SRE-STREAM-ERRORS fires, check streaming_active_sessions_metric and leaked_session_estimate (sum over session-keeper pods).
- Run: kubectl -n platform exec -it session-keeper-<pod> -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -s http://localhost:8080/metrics | grep leaked_sessions' to sample leaks per pod.
- If leaked_sessions > 50 on > 30% pods: initiate rolling restart sequence with stagger 30s and monitor leaked_sessions reduction.
- Soft mitigation: temporarily increase idle-eviction in redis/cache with CLI toggle: redis-cli SET session:evict_interval 15 (minutes -> 5) and notify cache-owners.
- If tcp_ephemeral_port_exhaustion observed on edge proxies: scale edge-proxy replicas and rotate nodes in pool.
- Communicate: post incident banner to #status with short explanation and ETA for official postmortem.

Post-incident notes (on-call reflections):
- The restart window was tight; early detection would have shortened outage by ~20–30 minutes. Our current streaming alerting relies on error-rate only; adding resource-usage signals would make detection earlier.
- Coordination with SDK team was effective once the reconnect behavior was identified; we should institute an SDK deployment checklist for changes that affect reconnect/backoff semantics.

Lessons learned:
1) Distinguish socket-level metrics from logical session metrics in alerts and dashboards.
2) Ensure autoscalers are gated on signals that reflect user-visible saturation.
3) Encourage SDKs to adopt randomized jitter by default for reconnects.
4) Add per-pod leak budget alerts to detect accumulation before global saturation.

Action items (owner / due / status):
- Add leaked_sessions metric and dashboard (Riley Chen / 2026-01-28 / in_progress).
- Fix disconnect cleanup in session-keeper and add unit + e2e tests (Daniel Park / 2026-02-05 / in_progress).
- Backport session-keeper patch to v2.14.x and ship emergency patch train (Daniel Park / 2026-01-25 / planned).
- SDK jitter re-enable + release + notify top 20 customers (Mateo Alvarez / 2026-01-20 / in_progress).
- Update SRE runbook with explicit rolling restart and cache-eviction steps (Priya Nair / 2026-01-26 / planned).

Blameless language reminder: This was a systems-level failure with multiple contributing factors. Postmortem focuses on fixes and process improvements, not individual fault.

Appendix: quick diagnostics checklist for future on-call
- Metrics to check immediately: streaming_active_sessions, leaked_sessions_per_pod, socket_fds_open, tcp_ephemeral_port_free_count, edge-proxy-accept-rate.
- Quick commands: kubectl logs --since=1h deployment/session-keeper | grep "onDisconnect" | tail -n 200; kubectl top pod -n platform | grep session-keeper
- Related artifacts: github.com/redwood-inference/stream-mux/pull/121 (bugfix), JIRA SRE-8764 (dashboard), INFRA-3421 (cleanup fix).

Owners of this doc: Aisha Khan (SRE lead) — please update with further learnings or customer impact notes.
